note: registry.yaml equivalent. JSON keeps the scanner to standard library plus requests, as section 1 requires. Every source named in section 2 has an entry. A source with verdict unresolved produces no rows and is not worked around, and is re-probed on each weekly run so its verdict does not go stale. last_status is the raw HTTP status the probe observed and is rewritten every run. It does not imply usable content: several blocked sites answer 200 with an interstitial. Only verdict decides whether a source is used, and verdict is changed by hand after a route has been read.

verdict_values.resolved: schedule page fetched at 200 and carries dated entries a plain fetcher can read
verdict_values.unresolved: no route found that satisfies the section 6 fetch gate

sources.name: Bank of England MPC dates
sources.route: One table per year under an h2 of the form '2026 confirmed dates'. First cell is the weekday and day and month, year from the heading. Second cell flags the Monetary Policy Report.
sources.yields: MPC rate decisions and Monetary Policy Report publication dates
sources.note: Announcement time is not on the page, so time is left blank.

sources.name: ECB Governing Council calendar
sources.route: Definition list of DD/MM/YYYY against a description. The decision is the day two entry that says it is followed by a press conference.
sources.note: Recovery against the historic run. That run failed on the ECB decisions index and the per year press release index, both of which render via JavaScript. This is a different page and is plain HTML.

sources.name: Federal Reserve FOMC calendar
sources.route: Meetings grouped under a '2026 FOMC Meetings' anchor, each a month label and a day range. The decision is the last day of the range.
sources.yields: FOMC decision dates, with the projections meetings flagged
sources.note: Forward minutes dates are not published on this page, so no minutes rows are written.

sources.name: ONS release calendar
sources.route: Upcoming filter, paged at 50. Each item carries data-gtm-release-date, data-gtm-release-time, the title and the release page link. The link is harvested and used as the source_url.
sources.yields: ONS consumer price inflation, labour market overview, monthly GDP and first quarterly GDP
sources.note: Release times are published here in UK civil time and are converted to UTC. The historic run could not find times on the bulletin pages, so trap B is captured going forward.

sources.name: BLS economic news release schedule
sources.route: Published iCalendar file. VEVENT blocks with DTSTART in US Eastern and the release name in SUMMARY.
sources.yields: US consumer price index and employment situation release dates and times
sources.note: Serves 200 as text/calendar from the same host whose HTML schedule pages return 403 or 404. The block is applied inconsistently and this URL returned 403 on one of four test fetches, so expect runs where it fails. Section 7 handles that by leaving the rows untouched with a stale last_verified. BLS API v1 was tested as the brief asks: it is open without a key but serves series observations, not release dates, so it does not recover the calendar.

sources.name: EIA weekly natural gas storage schedule
sources.route: Prose sentence giving the standard release day and time, then a table of holiday exceptions with alternate release dates and times.
sources.yields: holiday exception dates as published, ordinary weeks as generated
sources.note: The EIA publishes only its exceptions as dates. Ordinary weeks carry date_source=generated from the cadence sentence on the same page.

sources.name: EIA weekly petroleum status schedule
sources.route: Same shape as the gas storage schedule, with an extra leading column for the data week.
sources.yields: holiday exception dates as published, ordinary weeks as generated
sources.note: ir.eia.gov/wpsr/schedule.html returns 403. The www.eia.gov path carries the same table and is used instead.

sources.name: EIA Short Term Energy Outlook
sources.route: The outlook header states 'Next Release Date' as a single date.
sources.yields: one forward STEO release date per run
sources.note: Only one forward date exists on the page, so the series fills in month by month rather than arriving as a block.

sources.name: CFTC Commitments of Traders schedule
sources.route: A table per year under a '2026 Release Schedule' heading, one row per month with a cell per release day. The release time is stated in the prose above the table.
sources.yields: every weekly COT release date for the published year
sources.note: The page describes itself as a tentative schedule and marks holiday affected weeks with an asterisk, which is carried into notes.

sources.name: UK clock changes
sources.route: Table of year against the clocks go forward and clocks go back dates.
sources.note: Statutory, so it could be generated, but gov.uk publishes the dates so they are taken as published.

sources.name: IEA Oil Market Report and Gas Market Report
sources.note: iea.org returns 403 to a plain fetcher, as the historic run found. No route. Section 8 predicted this.

sources.name: OPEC monthly report, ministerials and JMMC
sources.note: opec.org serves the home page at 200 but returns 403 on /meetings.html, /events.html, /meeting-schedule.html and /press-releases.html. The home page carries past press releases only, no forward meeting dates.

sources.name: GIE AGSI gas storage
sources.note: 14 kB JavaScript shell with no dated content, unchanged from the historic run. The keyed API is out under decision 3.

sources.name: EU gas storage filling targets
sources.note: The page fetches at 200 and explains the regulation but carries no forward filling target dates as dated entries. Generating 1 November from the regulation text would be inference, so no row.

sources.name: Baker Hughes rig count
sources.note: rigcount.bakerhughes.com does not answer within 30 seconds on repeated attempts, at the root or on the rig count page.

sources.name: Ofgem price cap announcements
sources.note: Regression against the historic run, which listed ofgem.gov.uk as walking cleanly. The site now serves a BETA shell: 190 kB of markup that strips to about 7 kB of navigation, with no body content and no dated entries. The publications index behaves the same way.

sources.name: Capacity Market T-1 and T-4 auctions
sources.note: Every NESO capacity market path tried returns a soft 404 that serves a 1.2 MB error page. The EMR Delivery Body portal at emrdeliverybody.com is a login shell and states the Capacity Market has moved off it. The gov.uk capacity market collection carries publication dates, not forward auction dates.

sources.name: CfD allocation round milestones
sources.note: The collection fetches at 200 but its dates are document publication dates, not allocation round milestones. The EMR portal shows an application window closing date with no year attached, which fails the date on the page test.

sources.name: UK ETS auction calendar
sources.note: theice.com fetches at 200 but carries no dated auction entries in the markup. The auction calendar is distributed as a PDF.

sources.name: EU ETS auction calendar
sources.note: The page fetches at 200 and lists an 'EEX Auction Calendar 2026 (PDF)' with its publishing date, but the per auction dates are inside the PDF. The HTML carries document publishing dates only.

sources.name: EU Energy Council meetings
sources.note: consilium.europa.eu returns 403 on the meetings calendar and on the energy council path, as the historic run found. The weekly probe has recorded an occasional 200 which on inspection is an anti bot interstitial, not the calendar, so the verdict is unchanged.

sources.name: EU sectoral sanctions renewals
sources.note: finance.ec.europa.eu carries dated pages per adopted package, which is what the historic run used, but no forward renewal calendar. The six monthly renewal rhythm is real but the dates are not published in advance, so generating them would be forecasting.

sources.name: Budget and Spring Statement
sources.note: Neither the OBR nor the HM Treasury pages carry a forward fiscal event date as a dated entry. The date arrives as a written ministerial statement, which is a news item rather than a schedule.

sources.name: Annual network charging decisions
sources.note: Same Ofgem shell as the price cap. No dated entries reach a plain fetcher.

sources.name: Eurostat flash HICP and GDP
sources.note: The release calendar is a portlet that yields no per release dated links to a plain fetcher, unchanged from the historic run. Section 8 predicted this.

sources.name: PMIs for the UK, euro area, US and China
sources.note: spglobal.com is on the section 5 blocklist and was not built on. No alternative publisher of the PMI release calendar was found that carries dated entries.

sources.name: German Ifo and ZEW
sources.note: ifo.de serves a 3 kB shell with no content. zew.de times out on the indicator page and its press release index carries no forward dated entries.

sources.name: Scheduled elections and referendums
sources.note: The Commons Library briefing fetches at 200 but carries publication dates rather than a forward election timetable in dated form. electionresults.parliament.uk did not resolve by DNS.

sources.name: COP, G7, G20 and European Council
sources.note: unfccc.int returns a few hundred bytes on the calendar, conference and event calendar paths. g20.org carries no forward summit date as a dated entry. European Council dates sit on consilium.europa.eu, which is blocked.

sources.name: ICE contract expiries and prompt rolls
sources.note: The contract page fetches at 200 but the expiry calendar is not in the markup. Deriving expiries from the two business days before month end rule would be generation with no cadence sentence on a fetched page to stand behind it.

sources.name: Gas year start and the seasonal roll
sources.note: 1 October and 1 April are convention rather than a published schedule. No page was found that states them as dated entries, so no row. Omitting beats guessing.

sources.name: ECMWF and Copernicus monthly and seasonal outlooks
sources.note: Both sites fetch at 200 but publish past bulletins rather than a forward release calendar.

sources.name: Met Office three month outlook
sources.note: The contingency planners page fetches at 200 and carries no dated release schedule. The long range outlook paths tried return 404.

sources.name: NOAA hurricane season outlook
sources.note: The page carries the current outlook and its issue date but no forward schedule for the next issue.

sources.name: Physical supply schedules
sources.note: Norwegian field and pipeline maintenance, French nuclear availability, interconnector outages, LNG terminal maintenance and National Gas planned works are held back to phase two by section 2. Not attempted.
